From f8ef441811ec413717f188f63d99182f30f0f08e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Thomas Yen <thomasyen@google.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jan 2026 00:51:51 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] scsi: ufs: core: Flush exception handling work when RPM level
 is zero

Ensure that the exception event handling work is explicitly flushed during
suspend when the runtime power management level is set to UFS_PM_LVL_0.

When the RPM level is zero, the device power mode and link state both
remain active. Previously, the UFS core driver bypassed flushing exception
event handling jobs in this configuration. This created a race condition
where the driver could attempt to access the host controller to handle an
exception after the system had already entered a deep power-down state,
resulting in a system crash.

Explicitly flush this work and disable auto BKOPs before the suspend
callback proceeds. This guarantees that pending exception tasks complete
and prevents illegal hardware access during the power-down sequence.

Fixes: 57d104c153d3 ("ufs: add UFS power management support")
Signed-off-by: Thomas Yen <thomasyen@google.com>
Cc: Stable Tree <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Peter Wang <peter.wang@mediatek.com>
Reviewed-by: Bart Van Assche <bvanassche@acm.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260129165156.956601-1-thomasyen@google.com
Signed-off-by: Martin K. Petersen <martin.petersen@oracle.com>

diff --git a/drivers/ufs/core/ufshcd.c b/drivers/ufs/core/ufshcd.c
index 66223d290853..8349fe2090db 100644
--- a/drivers/ufs/core/ufshcd.c
+++ b/drivers/ufs/core/ufshcd.c
@@ -9998,6 +9998,8 @@ static int __ufshcd_wl_suspend(struct ufs_hba *hba, enum ufs_pm_op pm_op)
 
 	if (req_dev_pwr_mode == UFS_ACTIVE_PWR_MODE &&
 			req_link_state == UIC_LINK_ACTIVE_STATE) {
+		ufshcd_disable_auto_bkops(hba);
+		flush_work(&hba->eeh_work);
 		goto vops_suspend;
 	}
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

### Modifications in `drivers/ufs/core/ufshcd.c`

- **Location**: Inside `__ufshcd_wl_suspend()`, within the block that handles the case where the requested device power mode is `UFS_ACTIVE_PWR_MODE` and the requested link state is `UIC_LINK_ACTIVE_STATE` (i.e., RPM level is zero, meaning the device remains active during suspend).  
- **Added calls** immediately before the `goto vops_suspend`:
  1. `ufshcd_disable_auto_bkops(hba);` – Disables automatic background operations (BKOPs) to prevent new background tasks from starting during the suspend sequence.
  2. `flush_work(&hba->eeh_work);` – Flushes any pending exception event handling work, ensuring that any already queued exception tasks complete before the suspend proceeds.

### Relationship Between the Modifications

Both modifications work together to eliminate a race condition that occurs when the system suspends while the UFS device remains fully active (RPM level zero). Previously, exception event handling (e.g., for thermal or other urgent events) and background operations were not blocked or flushed in this code path. This allowed the driver to attempt to access the host controller hardware *after* the system had already powered down, causing a crash. By:
1. **Disabling auto BKOPs** – Prevents new background work from being scheduled.
2. **Flushing the exception work** – Ensures any already pending exception processing is completed synchronously.  
the driver guarantees that no further exception handling or background access will occur during the subsequent power-down sequence, thereby protecting against illegal hardware access.
